detail.longDescription: An Anthropic Mathematician Says Claude Helped Prove the Riemann Hypothesis A claim of proof, not yet a proof. Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, published a note on Friday saying he believes he has found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis — and that Claude did much of the finding. By his own account it took about six weeks with the model and ended with a formalization in Lean, the proof assistant, "without assumptions". He released the Lean files only, in fourteen parts, rather than a readable paper. He says a proper write-up is still to come. The problem itself: Bernhard Riemann, 1859, a question about how the primes fall along the number line. It is one of the Clay Institute's seven Millennium Prize problems, each worth $1m, and it has stood for nearly 170 years without an accepted proof. Why the Lean files carry the weight: - A formal proof can, in principle, be machine-checked. - Checking means confirming the theorems state what the note claims. - And that the derivation rests on standard axioms, not on one quietly added to close a gap. Alpöge is direct that the argument is unfinished as prose: it is "incredibly long at the moment", and he says he has "just taken a step" toward understanding it himself. He also expects the method to reach the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and with more time the Extended one. The timing drew attention before the mathematics did: the note appeared a day after Anthropic's Nasdaq debut. "The precise timing is horrible," he wrote, and rejected the cynical reading of it. Mathematicians have begun checking. The New York Times reported that an Italian mathematician, Alessandro Masullo, separately released an incomplete proof he had worked on for nearly 12 years, without AI because he does not fully trust it. Until reviewers finish, the honest description is a claim with a machine-checkable artifact attached. That is more than most announcements carry, and less than a solved problem. His note: alpo.ge/remark.pdf 📷 David Malone · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons 🔗 Source: The Guardian # AI # MachineLearning # LLM
